{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging" },
  "read": "The students who skipped the reading are probably avoiding the risk of looking unprepared or lost in front of peers — it feels safer to coast than to visibly struggle. The students who did the work are starting to feel like their effort doesn't matter, which is its own status injury.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Call out the unprepared half publicly or give a pop quiz as punishment — this shames the kids who are already avoidant and teaches the prepared kids that compliance is rewarded, not genuine engagement." },
  "mentorMove": "Acknowledge the imbalance without singling anyone out, reset the norm as a shared investment in the room working for everyone, and give the unprepared students a low-stakes on-ramp right now so they can contribute something real before the period ends.",
  "holdFirm": ["Coming prepared is the expectation every time, not optional.", "Discussion only works when everyone has skin in the game — that standard stays."],
  "stayFlexible": ["Let students who are behind do a quick one-minute silent skim or jot a question they have about the text before discussion resumes.", "Vary discussion formats so preparation shows up in more ways than just having the right answer ready."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "I'm going to pause us for a second. I can feel the energy in here getting uneven, and I think we all feel it." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Here's what I notice: some of you came in loaded and ready, and some of you are waiting to see where things go. I'm not going to make this awkward by asking who's who. But I am curious — what gets in the way of doing the reading before you walk in here?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here's what I want to try. Take ninety seconds right now, read just one paragraph or one page from wherever you can open it, and write down one genuine question you have. You don't need to have the answers — a real question is enough to get you into this conversation. The people who are prepared, I need you to hold that knowledge for sixty more seconds." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I hold you all to coming prepared because I have high standards for what this class can actually do together, and I've seen enough from every single one of you to know you're capable of it. When half the room is carrying the other half, we're leaving a lot of thinking on the table. Let's get it all on the table." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Build a quick low-stakes accountability ritual — an opening written response, a text-to-self jot, anything that makes preparation visible and useful before discussion starts, so readiness becomes the social norm rather than optional."
}
situation: Half the class did the reading and half clearly did not, and the half that did is getting visibly annoyed at carrying discussions.
